@sepo-agent /answer 

How to redesign the website such that it can support 
1. switch to a previous year, /2025/ etc 
2. also update to the new year version /2026?

comments.body:
Here's a concrete plan for supporting year-based versioning (`/2025/`, `/2026/`) on this Nextra 4 + Next.js 15 site.

---

## Current architecture

The site uses **Nextra 4 (RC)** with `contentDirBasePath: '/docs'`. All content lives flat in `src/content/` and routes to `/docs/*`. There are no year-based folders yet.

Key files:
- [`next.config.ts`](https://github.com/lm4sci/lm4sci.github.io/blob/main/next.config.ts) — sets `contentDirBasePath: '/docs'`
- [`src/app/_meta.js`](https://github.com/lm4sci/lm4sci.github.io/blob/main/src/app/_meta.js) — top-level page/route declarations
- [`src/content/_meta.js`](https://github.com/lm4sci/lm4sci.github.io/blob/main/src/content/_meta.js) — sidebar nav for current content
- [`src/app/docs/[[...mdxPath]]/page.jsx`](https://github.com/lm4sci/lm4sci.github.io/blob/main/src/app/docs/%5B%5B...mdxPath%5D%5D/page.jsx) — catch-all MDX route

---

## Proposed approach

### Option A — Year subfolders under `/docs/` (simplest, recommended)

Nest content by year inside the existing `/docs` base path:

```
src/content/
├── _meta.js           ← top-level: points to 2025/, 2026/
├── 2025/
│   ├── _meta.js       ← sidebar nav for 2025
│   ├── index.mdx
│   ├── organizers.mdx
│   ├── call-for-papers.mdx
│   ├── schedule.mdx
│   └── faq.mdx
└── 2026/
    ├── _meta.js
    ├── index.mdx
    └── ...
```

URLs produced: `/docs/2025/`, `/docs/2025/schedule`, `/docs/2026/`, etc.

Nextra resolves `_meta.js` recursively, so the sidebar will automatically show a collapsible year section. No changes to `next.config.ts` or the dynamic route are needed.

### Option B — Year as the top-level path segment (cleaner URLs, more work)

Route directly to `/2025/` and `/2026/` without the `/docs` prefix. This requires:
1. Changing `contentDirBasePath` in `next.config.ts` to `'/'` (or adding parallel route groups in `src/app/`)
2. Adding year-level entries in `src/app/_meta.js`
3. Possibly duplicating or parameterizing the `[[...mdxPath]]` catch-all

This gives nicer URLs but is a bigger structural change. It also risks breaking the existing `/docs` path if not redirected.

---

## Recommended step-by-step plan (Option A)

1. **Move 2025 content** into `src/content/2025/` — rename existing MDX files in place.
2. **Add `src/content/2025/_meta.js`** — copy current `_meta.js`, no changes needed.
3. **Update `src/content/_meta.js`** — replace flat page list with year entries:
   ```js
   export default {
     2026: { title: '2026' },
     2025: { title: '2025 (Archive)' },
   }
   ```
4. **Create `src/content/2026/`** — new year's content with its own `_meta.js`.
5. **Update `src/app/layout.jsx`** — optionally add a year switcher in the Navbar (a simple dropdown or links to `/docs/2026` vs `/docs/2025`).
6. **Add redirects** — in `next.config.ts`, redirect `/docs` → `/docs/2026` so the current year is the default landing page.
7. **Update image/asset paths** — move year-specific images under `public/images/2025/` to avoid collisions.

---

## Open questions before implementing

1. **URL preference**: Do you want `/docs/2026/` (Option A) or clean `/2026/` (Option B)?
2. **Default year redirect**: Should `/docs` or `/` redirect to the latest year automatically, or should the root page be a landing that lists all years?
3. **Year switcher UI**: Should the navbar show a year dropdown, or is a sidebar section sufficient?
4. **Content reuse**: Are any components (e.g., `OrganizerGrid`, `Collapsible`) expected to differ between years, or stay shared?

Let me know your preference on URL structure and I can start the implementation.

1. ok we might need to update the landing page? https://lm4sci.github.io/
2. can we just rename current docs/ to 2025/ and we can add 2026 as the default navigation ? 
3. `Year switcher UI: Should the navbar show a year dropdown, or is a sidebar section sufficient?` -> we should add a section on landing page for past years ? Also in the 2026 docs we should add a seciton 
4. Let's not worry about content reuse yet

@sepo-agent /answer

Good — here's the concrete plan aligned to your preferences.

---

## What changes, file by file

### 1. Move all current content into `src/content/2025/`

```
src/content/2025/
├── _meta.js           ← copy of current _meta.js (no changes needed)
├── index.mdx
├── organizers.mdx
├── call-for-papers.mdx
├── schedule.mdx
└── faq.mdx
```

URLs become: `/docs/2025/`, `/docs/2025/schedule`, etc.

---

### 2. Create `src/content/2026/` as the new default

```
src/content/2026/
├── _meta.js           ← same shape, updated titles/links for 2026
├── index.mdx          ← new overview + link to past years at bottom
├── organizers.mdx     ← placeholder (or copy + update from 2025)
├── call-for-papers.mdx
├── schedule.mdx
└── faq.mdx
```

Add a "Past Editions" entry at the bottom of `2026/_meta.js` using Nextra's separator + external link pattern:

```js
export default {
  index: { title: 'Overview' },
  organizers: { title: 'Organizers' },
  'call-for-papers': { title: 'Call for Papers' },
  schedule: { title: 'Schedule' },
  faq: { title: 'FAQ' },
  '---': { type: 'separator', title: 'Archive' },
  '2025-link': { title: 'LM4Sci 2025 ↗', href: '/docs/2025' },
}
```

---

### 3. Update `src/content/_meta.js` (top-level)

```js
export default {
  2026: { title: 'LM4Sci 2026' },
  2025: { title: 'LM4Sci 2025' },
}
```

---

### 4. Update `src/app/page.jsx` (landing page)

Three changes:
- **Hero panel** (`line 64`): change "LM4Sci 2025" → "LM4Sci 2026", update date/location once known (or leave as TBD)
- **CTA buttons** (`lines 41–54`): update `/docs` → `/docs/2026` and `/docs/call-for-papers` → `/docs/2026/call-for-papers`
- **Schedule link** (`line 356`): `/docs/schedule` → `/docs/2026/schedule`
- **Important Dates section** (`lines 364–405`): update to 2026 dates, or replace with TBD placeholders
- **Add "Past Editions" section** before the CTA block: a simple card/link grid pointing to `/docs/2025`

---

### 5. No redirect needed (static export)

Since the site uses `output: 'export'`, server-side redirects don't work. Instead, update every `/docs` link in `page.jsx` to `/docs/2026` explicitly — this is cleaner anyway. The top-level `/docs` route (if visited directly) will show Nextra's year-chooser sidebar automatically.

---

## Questions before I start

1. **2026 content**: Do you want the 2026 files to start as copies of 2025 (placeholder), or should I create minimal stubs (just frontmatter + "Coming soon")?
2. **Important Dates for 2026**: Do you have dates to fill in, or should I use TBD placeholders?
3. **Hero section**: Keep "co-located with COLM" as the venue or leave blank for 2026?

Give me the go-ahead (and any date/venue info if you have it) and I'll implement all of this.

Implemented year-based content versioning for the LM4Sci site. Moved all existing 2025 content (index, organizers, call-for-papers, schedule, faq, _meta.js) into src/content/2025/. Created minimal 2026 stub files under src/content/2026/ (overview with COLM '26 date/location, plus Coming Soon pages for organizers, CfP, schedule, FAQ).
